correspondence.component_scope: Chosen unnamed feeder and Indian Creek canyon
correspondence.finding: The chosen northwestern opening descends a minor canyon on the eastern Animas Mountains flank and enters the southward Indian Creek corridor below the Broom Canyon surroundings. The relief, enclosing slopes and directly labeled receiving channel identify the same feeder-to-canyon setting. The selected line then continues along Indian Creek toward its Deer Creek junction.
correspondence.name_scope: The opening itself remains unnamed; Indian Creek applies to the directly labeled receiving canyon.

correspondence.component_scope: Indian Creek junction and southward Deer Creek canyon
correspondence.finding: The Indian corridor meets the west-arriving Deer Creek corridor, and the selection continues southeast through the same valley beside the repeated Deer Creek labels. Black Creek and the other lateral canyon mouths are visible context; none is substituted for the chosen opening. Overlapping originals cover the junction, successive bends and the lower canyon.
correspondence.name_scope: Deer Creek is supported for this selected canyon reach; unselected western headwaters are not included by inference.

correspondence.component_scope: Deer Creek bend, Whitewater receiving junction and northern valley entry
correspondence.finding: The mapped Deer Creek corridor turns east around the southern Smuggler Hills, receives Whitewater Creek from the southwest, and bends north onto the adjoining Upper Playas receiving floor. The southern original shows the full U-shaped canyon exit and northward continuation, not merely separate nearby name labels.
correspondence.name_scope: Deer Creek remains the directly supported component name; Whitewater Creek is an unselected joining tributary.

correspondence.component_scope: Deer Creek fan and Upper Playas axial transition
correspondence.finding: Beyond the mountain front the route continues north through one broad alluvial floor, alongside the Deer and Brushy creek terminal reaches and across the highway setting. The original maps cover the entire fan-to-axis transition and tributary-fan mouths. The road log independently identifies the northward Upper Playas axial drainage. No exact wetted channel through each dry patch is asserted.
correspondence.name_scope: South Playas Draw is supported at broad axial-drainage scale. Deer Creek and Brushy Creek labels are not extended over the entire valley.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Playas northward floor beside the Big Hatchet Mountains
correspondence.finding: The selection continues along the low alluvial axis west of the Big Hatchet Mountains, passing road grids and scattered small water features before turning northeast toward the low passage north of the range. Overlapping originals cover the entire valley corridor and both sides of the highway. The road log identifies this Upper Playas drainage and distinguishes its principal northern receiving basin from its branch through Hatchet Gap.
correspondence.name_scope: South Playas Draw is a supported authorial axial identity, with no precise name-boundary vertex assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Hatchet Gap surface-spill passage
correspondence.finding: The route turns east through the low gap immediately north of the Big Hatchet Mountains. Topographic relief depicts the passage and the eastern receiving corridor; imagery covers its eastern outlet. The independent road log explicitly identifies Hatchet Gap between the Big and Little Hatchet ranges as a surface-water spill passage from Playas Valley into Hachita Valley. This establishes the geographic through-link without requiring current overflow.
correspondence.name_scope: Hatchet Gap is a geographic passage, not a river hydronym. The distinct Playas and Hachita basin identities are retained.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward and southeastward Hachita receiving corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor follows the same low passage east from the gap and then southeast between the Big Hatchet piedmont and the Sierra Rica side. Topographic relief and the imagery show a continuous incised-to-alluvial, vegetated drainage corridor with lateral tributary entries, continuing to the international boundary. The road log names Hachita Draw as the axial drainage and identifies the receiving Moscos depression.
correspondence.name_scope: Hachita Draw is supported for the receiving Hachita drainage at ordinary corridor scale; the name is not applied to the entire upstream Playas composite.

correspondence.component_scope: International boundary, cultivated floor and playa approach
correspondence.finding: The same southeastern corridor crosses the international boundary and reaches the irrigated-field and branching-drainage setting on the Mexican alluvial floor. The image shows the downstream pale, channel-marked receiving floor continuously between the field margins and the terminal playa. This is one receiving setting, not an unsupported transfer to a separate basin; current farm routing and any exact channel through a particular field are not inferred.
correspondence.name_scope: The Hachita–Moscos receiving setting is supported. No new canal name or extension of a tributary name over the fields is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual endpoint on the Laguna Los Moscos receiving playa
correspondence.finding: The final southeastward continuation remains within the same low receiving depression and ends on its northern playa floor. The original imagery covers the actual endpoint, beyond the cultivated approach, amid the pale playa surface and darker wet-ground patches. The authorial description identifies this Hachita receiving depression as the Laguna Los Moscos ephemeral lake plain.
correspondence.name_scope: Laguna Los Moscos is the receiving lake-plain/depression name, kept separate from river hydronyms and without a current waterline claim.

correspondence.component_scope: Twin Piñon Gulch opening, northeastern fan and axial-wash join
correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies in the eastern mountain-front ravine labeled Twin Piñon Gulch. The original overview depicts its northeastward feeder channel and direct meeting with the north-trending axial wash; the southern detail depicts the enclosing ravine, low fan and adjoining broad wash floor. The initial generalized bends stay within that gulch-to-fan corridor.
correspondence.name_scope: Twin Piñon Gulch is a bounded geographic gulch label, not a scalar name for the selected river system. The downstream axial wash is unnamed here.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern Little Smoky axial wash and Big Fault/Snowball tributary entries
correspondence.finding: The route turns north along the same low axial wash between the western fans and the eastern uplands. The overview depicts the connected intermittent channel and the entries of Big Fault Wash and Snowball Creek from the west. The detailed original depicts the continuous elongated wash/playa floor and the same receiving joins. No separate closed-basin transfer is selected at these joins.
correspondence.name_scope: Big Fault Wash and Snowball Creek are tributary context; their western headwaters are not the selected opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Willow Creek receiving reach, Willow Creek Spring and axial wet-ground continuation
correspondence.finding: The western Willow Creek joins the selected axial corridor. In the detailed original, repeated Willow Creek labels follow its eastward approach and bounded northward receiving bend; the selected route then continues through the same elongated wash/wet-ground floor past Willow Creek Spring. The overview supplies the continuous axial channel where detailed blue linework is sparse.
correspondence.name_scope: Willow Creek is supported for the bounded receiving interval. Willow Creek Spring is a separate spring, and neither name is extended to the whole selected path.

correspondence.component_scope: Cockalorum Wash receiving floor and northward approach to Fish Creek
correspondence.finding: The selected route passes the Cockalorum Wash entry and continues north through the long Fish Creek Valley lowland to the east-west Fish Creek corridor. The overview depicts the axial channel and its receiving junction; the overlapping southern and middle details cover the same low floor, roads and local cultivated setting. The selected northern approach reaches Fish Creek east of its spring headwaters.
correspondence.name_scope: Cockalorum Wash is adjoining tributary context. This northward axial interval is unnamed in the inspected cartography.

correspondence.component_scope: Fish Creek join and eastward receiving reach
correspondence.finding: At the end of the northward axial approach, the selection turns east into the directly labeled Fish Creek corridor and crosses the road setting before bending northeast. The original detailed cartography distinguishes the Fish Creek Springs headwater branches to the west from this selected southern feeder, and shows the receiving river through their meeting.
correspondence.name_scope: Fish Creek is directly supported on the selected receiving trunk. Unselected western spring branches and South Fork Fish Creek are not substituted for the chosen opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Fish Creek northeastward outlet toward Newark Valley
correspondence.finding: The selected route continues northeast in the same Fish Creek corridor along the low passage between the Fish Creek Range side and Pancake Range foothills. The overview labels the trunk and depicts its joined drainage; the detail covers the bends, surrounding low relief and Little Smoky Valley outlet setting. Rush and Everett independently describe Fish Creek leaving the northern valley unit for Newark Valley, with ephemeral surface outflow.
correspondence.name_scope: Fish Creek is the supported receiving-system identity. The historical outflow statement establishes the geographic passage, without requiring current water or continuous base flow.

correspondence.component_scope: Highway crossing and southern Newark Valley axial continuation
correspondence.finding: The route crosses the east-west highway setting and continues north-northeast through the southern Newark Valley lowland. The overview depicts the continuous intermittent axial channel and surrounding tributary entries. Middle and northern details show the same open receiving floor between the mountain fronts and the local roads; no separate ridge crossing or interbasin spillway is selected.
correspondence.name_scope: The selected downstream axial interval is not given an additional river name. Its connection to the named Fish Creek outlet is supported geographically.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern valley channel and Newark Lake southern tongue
correspondence.finding: The northward axial channel leads into the narrow southern tongue of the large Newark Lake playa. The overview maps this receiving channel and the playa together; the northern detail shows the enclosing low contours and uninterrupted tongue-to-main-playa setting. The selected bend into the southern playa is covered.
correspondence.name_scope: Newark Lake is a separate terminal lake/playa identity; it is not a river-name extension.

correspondence.component_scope: Newark Lake interior passage
correspondence.finding: The selection continues north through the interior of the long mapped Newark Lake playa, including its narrower northern neck and irregular margins. Original cartography continuously covers the receiving floor. Dry patches and islands within this one lake/playa setting do not require a continuously drawn or presently wetted river thread.
correspondence.name_scope: Newark Lake is directly labeled in the northern original. No additional stream or lake name is invented for individual patches.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected endpoint inside northern Newark Lake
correspondence.finding: The last selected bends remain inside the northern part of the same Newark Lake playa. The actual endpoint is covered by both map scales and lies within the lake/playa interior, beyond the southern lake entry and main body. The selection does not continue to the entire northern limit of the mapped lake.
correspondence.name_scope: Newark Lake is the supported actual terminal receiving feature. Fish Creek remains a representative receiving-system name, not a scalar lake name.

correspondence.component_scope: chosen opening
correspondence.finding: The selected inland opening is on the Kiahara-side forested drainage in the savanna south of Waspam. The narrow opening and its east-northeast corridor correspond to the mapped Kiahara tributary and the continuous wooded drainage visible in imagery. No lake or reservoir is selected at the opening.

correspondence.component_scope: kiahara confluence and middle ulang
correspondence.finding: The Kiahara corridor reaches the confluence with the larger northern river and continues southeast along the Ulang floodplain. The atlas labels Kiahara and Ulang separately; the dictionary independently describes Kiahara as an Ulang tributary. Selected model mainstem role is retained even where the natural headward reach has its own name.

correspondence.component_scope: lower ulang wetland approach
correspondence.finding: The selected southern turn leaves the eastward coastal branch and follows the shared, continuously visible vegetated wetland corridor toward northern Pahra. The atlas depicts this lowland drainage setting; Incer explicitly places the Ulang outlet in Páhara. The correspondence is supported by the actual receiving corridor and authorial connection, rather than proximity of basin labels alone.

correspondence.component_scope: fragment join and lagoon entry
correspondence.finding: The stage-3 to stage-2 fragment join lies in the northern Pahra receiving wetland and lagoon-entry setting. Image coverage is continuous across the join and shows channels, small wetland pools and the broad northern lagoon; no separate unsupported intercomponent transfer remains.

correspondence.component_scope: lagoon traversal
correspondence.finding: The selected lower fragment crosses the northern and central open-water reaches of Laguna Pahra, called Páhara in Incer, then continues into the southern narrowing. The lake name is a distinct receiving-water name and is not assigned as a river alias.

correspondence.component_scope: southern outlet and actual ending
correspondence.finding: The selected ending lies along the lagoon’s southern tidal outlet and adjacent Caribbean barrier-shore setting. The Auastara village/bar geographic context is independently described by Incer. The supplied source endpoint and separate rendered sea-class endpoint are preserved; the observed coastal passage is not claimed to put either point at an exact present-day open mouth.

correspondence.component_scope: managed passages and other components
correspondence.finding: No selected reservoir, dam crossing or independently identifiable managed transfer is required to connect these fragments. Minor bends, wetland pools and coastal bar morphology are treated within the continuously covered drainage and receiving-water setting, without present-flow or engineering-operation claims.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen eastern headward opening and northward valley between the Turkey Knob and Round Hill surroundings
correspondence.finding: The detailed topographic original locates the chosen opening within the northward-opening low corridor on the eastern side of the Cedar Mountain surroundings. The paired imagery shows the valley and branching dry drainage continuing toward its widening northern exit. Small cloud patches affect part of the image near the opening, but the independent topographic view supplies the enclosed valley and opening geography. No separate hydronym is established for this feeder.
correspondence.name_scope: Unnamed headward feeder component, not a verified Lordsburg Draw name boundary.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward upper alluvial plain and passage around The Saltys
correspondence.finding: The opening map and imagery show the selected westward bend within the same pale, low alluvial receiving belt, continuing around the northern side of the small hills labeled The Saltys and then into the southwestern low ground. The selected floor receives several minor northward and lateral washes. Road crossings lie within that continuous valley/plain setting. No intervening ridge or separate closed basin is required by the source correspondence.
correspondence.name_scope: Unnamed upper wash and receiving floor; The Saltys is a hill/locality label, not a candidate river name.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestward floor, northwestern turn and entry to the Burro Cienaga collector
correspondence.finding: The imagery follows the broad dry channel/fan belt westward past the small hachured waterbody setting and north of the Brockman Hills, then northwest into the more clearly incised collector beside the Homestead Hill surroundings. The topographic originals identify the receiving corridor as Burro Cienaga and show the nearby Ninetysix Creek junction and other tributary entries. Diffuse individual threads do not interrupt the visibly continuous receiving-floor geography.
correspondence.name_scope: Unnamed upper component entering Burro Cienaga; Ninetysix Creek is an entering tributary, not an alias or separate selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Burro Cienaga northwestern valley and approach to the pond/flat complex southeast of Lordsburg
correspondence.finding: Repeated Burro Cienaga labels identify the northwestern collector on the valley floor east of the Pyramid Mountains. The mapped corridor receives small side draws and crosses local roads while remaining in the same broad lowland. The selected route continues into the adjacent open-water and hachured-flat complex south of Interstate 10. The 2000 field-road-log prose independently identifies Burro Cienega as a major tributary of Lordsburg Draw.
correspondence.name_scope: Burro Cienaga is the map spelling; Burro Cienega is the road-log spelling. Both are retained at this tributary-component scope without asserting a formal registry alias.

correspondence.component_scope: Pond/flat complex and northwestern highway/rail corridor
correspondence.finding: Overlapping middle and lower maps show the selected shallow-water/flat surroundings and their continuous northwestern continuation through the Interstate 10 and railroad setting toward Lordsburg. The report describes the valley axis as indistinct, discontinuous drainage on an alkali-flat plain. This is a connected lowland passage at ordinary geographic scale; no exact managed conduit, culvert, individual pond outlet or currently wetted thread is assigned.
correspondence.name_scope: Receiving plain associated with the Burro Cienaga–Lordsburg Draw system; the small waterbodies remain unnamed in this finding.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestern passage around the north side of Lordsburg
correspondence.finding: The lower map and overview carry the selected lowland north of Lordsburg and around the northern end of the surrounding hills. Trauger's authorial drainage description explicitly identifies the valley's ill-defined axial watercourse as Lordsburg Draw and describes its northwestward course around the north of town before turning southwest. Together they establish the broad through-passage without requiring blue stream linework across every dry plain interval.
correspondence.name_scope: Lordsburg Draw representative axial corridor, with no precise name-change point imposed on the upstream component.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestern Lordsburg Draw approach to the alkali flat
correspondence.finding: The lower original directly labels Lordsburg Draw on the broad southwestern receiving corridor east of the large southern alkali flat. The selected approach lies within the continuous low ground north of the highway and enters the eastern/northeastern margin of that flat. This agrees with the report's southwestward continuation from Lordsburg toward the closed Lower Animas receiving basin.
correspondence.name_scope: Lordsburg Draw lower approach, distinct from the name of the terminal flat.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual terminal continuation within South Alkali Flat
correspondence.finding: The selected terminal turns and endpoint remain within the large southern hachured playa that the lower original labels South Alkali Flat. The neighboring northern playa is separate and is not substituted for the actual endpoint. Trauger's historical prose calls the receiving waterbody South Alkali Lake and places it in the closed Lower Animas Valley. The final display continuation is assessed as receiving-floor geography rather than a river channel traced across the dry lake bed.
correspondence.name_scope: South Alkali Flat, cartographic terminal feature; South Alkali Lake, historical report wording for the receiving lake. Neither is a scalar alias for the selected river group.
